content:
We just published a list of the 10 Best Growth Stocks for the Next 5 Years and Block (NYSE:XYZ) ranked 10th on this list.

Technology stocks went from celebration to rout within two sessions this month. On Wednesday, November 4, equities rallied after Democrats swept Congress in the midterm elections. By Thursday, the S&P 500 had fallen 4.36% and the Dow had lost 3.44%, while the Nasdaq Composite closed 5.52% lower, its worst day since April 2025. The drop pushed the tech-heavy index into correction territory, at least 10% below its October 6 record close.

The selling did not stop there, and the S&P 500 went on to post its worst week since June. Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner called the action "something of a buyers' strike" in technology. Breadth was thin, with only about one in seven S&P 500 stocks rising on the day of the steepest decline.

Photo by osamu nakazawa on Unsplash

A Midterm Shock Rattles the Market's Growth Engine

The election result mattered for reasons that go beyond party control. eToro market analyst Jakub Rochlitz said rising electricity prices turned data-center construction into a political issue during the campaign. In his view, markets now assume that the artificial intelligence buildout will be slower and more expensive, which rewrites growth expectations for every company along the supply chain.

The damage was sharpest in semiconductors. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12% and the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4%, the biggest one-day declines for both gauges since March 2020. Readers following the group can find more names in our list of the most promising technology stocks to buy right now .

Rising Rates and Heavy Debt Put Growth Valuations to the Test

Anxiety about AI spending had been building well before the vote. Bloomberg reported that interest rates were climbing, borrowing to fund the buildout was growing, and public backlash against data centers was spreading. Investors are now demanding higher yields from heavily indebted data-center builders, which raises the cost of every new project.

The numbers show how quickly sentiment turned. An October 30 sell-off erased more than $1 trillion of tech market value, and chipmakers surrendered more than $1.5 trillion on November 5 alone. Analyst-driven picks from the same corner of the market are collected in our list of the best aggressive growth stocks to buy according to Wall Street analysts .

Not everyone read the move as a break in the trend. Argent Capital Management portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek told Reuters that the selling felt like capitulation among the beneficiaries of data-center spending, though the size of the move looked outsized to him. His comment shows that even investors who saw capitulation in data-center names questioned the scale of the decline.

Block made it to our list because it has a five-year EPS growth rate of 36.61% and an average upside potential of 18%.

Investors cheered Block's third-quarter report because growth finally showed up in profit. Adjusted operating income climbed 92%, and the shares surged the next day. Block runs Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, and both contributed. Square's gross payment volume grew at its fastest pace since early 2023, while Cash App lending originations rose 40%, a sign that the consumer side is leaning into credit.

Bank of America analyst Matthew O'Neill reaffirmed a Buy rating on November 4 and raised his price target to $117 from $115. He said the quality of growth continues to improve, and he is positive on early 2027, when management expects gross profit to grow 15%. That view matters because the company has spent years being judged on how efficiently it turns gross profit into earnings.

Costs remain the open question. A Justice Department accrual weighed on reported results, and GAAP operating income grew far more slowly than the adjusted figure. Our analysis of how Block's lending-led gross profit growth squares with its costs takes up that question, including what the shift in mix means for margins.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of XYZ as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .
